He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it, when a snake sprang upon us. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Kill it.' We rushed at it, but it escaped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'It has been protected from your evil, just as you have been protected from its evil.'"

Muslim also narrated it through the route of al-A'mash [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1830), and Sahih Muslim no. (2234)].

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, from his mother: that she heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting "Wal-Mursalat 'Urfa" in the Maghrib prayer [al-Musnad (6/338)].

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs through the route of Malik, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (763), and Sahih Muslim no. (462)].

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Zakariya ibn Sahl al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," he said: "The angels."

He said: It was also related from Masruq, Abu al-Duha, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, something similar.

It was related from Abu Salih that he said: "They are the messengers." In another narration from him: "They are the angels." Abu Salih also said the same regarding "al-'Asifat," "al-Nashirat" [and "al-Fariqat"] (addition from A), and "al-Mulqiyat": that they are the angels.

Al-Thawri said, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," and he said: "The wind." Ibn Jarir refrained from deciding regarding "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," whether they are the angels when sent with ma'ruf (goodness), or like the ma'ruf (mane) of a horse, where some follow others, or they are the winds when they blow gradually, bit by bit. He definitively held that "al-'Asifati 'asfa" are the winds, as Ibn Mas'ud and those who followed him said. Among those who also said this regarding "al-'Asifat" were Ali ibn Abi Talib [in A: "Ali ibn Abi Talhah"], and al-Suddi. He refrained regarding "wal-Nashirati nashra," whether they are the angels or the wind, as previously mentioned. And from Abu Salih: that "al-Nashirat nashra" is the rain.

The more apparent view is that "al-Mursalat" are the winds, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We send the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57]. Likewise, "al-'Asifat" are the winds; it is said "'asafat al-rih" when the wind blows with sound. Likewise, "al-Nashirat" are the winds that spread the clouds across the horizons of the sky, as the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then those that separate, separating, Then those that deliver a reminder, as an excuse or a warning﴾, it means: the angels. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and al-Thawri. * *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is surely to occur﴾, this is what is sworn to by these oaths, that is: what you have been promised of the Hour's establishment, the blowing into the Trumpet, the resurrection of bodies, the gathering of the first and the last in one place, and the recompense of every doer for his deed, whether good with good or evil with evil. All of this is ﴿surely to occur﴾, meaning: it will undoubtedly come to pass.

Then He said: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, meaning: their light will be extinguished, like His saying: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾ [al-Takwir: 2], and His saying: ﴿And when the planets are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar: 2].

﴿And when the heaven is split open﴾, meaning: it will be cleft and torn asunder, its edges will hang down, and its extremities will become weak.

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, meaning: they will be carried off so that no trace or sign of them remains, like His saying: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blast, and leave it a level, smooth plain, in which you will see no crookedness or curvature﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105–107], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the day We set the mountains moving, and you see the earth laid bare, and We gather them, and leave none of them behind﴾ [al-Kahf: 47].

* *

Ibn Zayd said: this is like His saying: ﴿The day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. Mujahid said: ﴿Uqqitat﴾ means "postponed to a term" (ujjilat).

Al-Thawri narrated from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿Uqqitat﴾ means "were threatened" (awida'at). It seems he takes it like His saying: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord, and the Book is placed, and the prophets and the witnesses are brought, and judgment is given between them with truth, and they are not wronged﴾ [al-Zumar: 69].

As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So do not think that Allah would break His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution, on the day the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens as well, and they will come out before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim: 47–48]. And it is the Day of Decision, as He said: ﴿for the Day of Decision﴾.

Then He said, magnifying its matter: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Decision is? Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, meaning: woe to them from the punishment of Allah tomorrow. We have previously mentioned in a hadith that "Wayl" is a valley in Hell, but this is not authentic.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 77, verses 1–15:

Tafsir of Surah al-Mursalat

It is Meccan.

Al-Bukhari said: Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, [my father narrated to us] (addition from M, A, and al-Bukhari), al-A'mash narrated to us, Ibrahim narrated to me, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "While we were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave at Mina, the surah 'Wal-Mursalat' was revealed to him. He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it, when a snake sprang upon us. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Kill it.' We rushed at it, but it escaped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'It has been protected from your evil, just as you have been protected from its evil.'"

Muslim also narrated it through the route of al-A'mash [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1830), and Sahih Muslim no. (2234)].

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, from his mother: that she heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting "Wal-Mursalat 'Urfa" in the Maghrib prayer [al-Musnad (6/338)].

In the narration of Malik, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abbas: that Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting: "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," and she said: "O my son, you reminded me by your recitation of this surah that it was the last thing I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting in it in the Maghrib prayer."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs through the route of Malik, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (763), and Sahih Muslim no. (462)].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Zakariya ibn Sahl al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," he said: "The angels."

He said: It was also related from Masruq, Abu al-Duha, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, something similar.

It was related from Abu Salih that he said: "They are the messengers." In another narration from him: "They are the angels." Abu Salih also said the same regarding "al-'Asifat," "al-Nashirat" [and "al-Fariqat"] (addition from A), and "al-Mulqiyat": that they are the angels.

Al-Thawri said, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," and he said: "The wind." He likewise said regarding "Fal-'Asifati 'asfa wal-nashirati nashra" that they are the wind. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abu Salih (in one narration from him) likewise said so. Ibn Jarir refrained from deciding regarding "Wal-Mursalati 'Urfa," whether they are the angels when sent with ma'ruf (goodness), or like the ma'ruf (mane) of a horse, where some follow others, or they are the winds when they blow gradually, bit by bit. He definitively held that "al-'Asifati 'asfa" are the winds, as Ibn Mas'ud and those who followed him said. Among those who also said this regarding "al-'Asifat" were Ali ibn Abi Talib [in A: "Ali ibn Abi Talhah"], and al-Suddi. He refrained regarding "wal-Nashirati nashra," whether they are the angels or the wind, as previously mentioned. And from Abu Salih: that "al-Nashirat nashra" is the rain.

The more apparent view is that "al-Mursalat" are the winds, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We send the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57]. Likewise, "al-'Asifat" are the winds; it is said "'asafat al-rih" when the wind blows with sound. Likewise, "al-Nashirat" are the winds that spread the clouds across the horizons of the sky, as the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then those that separate, separating, Then those that deliver a reminder, as an excuse or a warning﴾, it means: the angels. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and al-Thawri. There is no disagreement here: they descend by the command of Allah to the messengers, distinguishing between truth and falsehood, guidance and error, the lawful and the unlawful, and they convey to the messengers a revelation which contains an excuse to creation and a warning to them of the punishment of Allah should they oppose His command.

* *

All of this is ﴿surely to occur﴾, meaning: it will undoubtedly come to pass.

Then He said: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, meaning: their light will be extinguished, like His saying: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾ [al-Takwir: 2], and His saying: ﴿And when the planets are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar: 2].

﴿And when the heaven is split open﴾, meaning: it will be cleft and torn asunder, its edges will hang down, and its extremities will become weak.

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, meaning: they will be carried off so that no trace or sign of them remains, like His saying: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Then He says, reminding His creatures of His favour and arguing for the resurrection from the fact of the first creation: ﴿Did We not create you from a despicable fluid?﴾ That is, weak and insignificant compared with the power of the Creator, the Originator, Mighty and Majestic. [[The takhrij of this hadith was mentioned in the commentary on verse 26 of Surah al-Qiyamah.]].

﴿Then We placed it in a firm repository.﴾ That is, We lodged it in the womb, which is the resting place of the fluid from the man and the woman. The womb is prepared for this purpose and keeps safe what is deposited in it of the fluid.

* *
